source_name: ICT Cortex - Montenegrin ICT cluster (member directory, news, open positions)
why_relevant: Cluster of ~40 Montenegrin ICT companies; publishes member profiles, aggregated open positions of member companies and business-performance analyses. It is the single best actor map for domestic integrators that could be serving banks, and its job-openings posts are a hiring signal aggregator.

source_name: Asseco SEE / Asseco group Montenegro-facing products (NLB Klik / ProKlik ME mobile apps, Google Play listings)
why_relevant: Play Store package names expose the vendor behind a Montenegrin bank's digital channel (e.g. NLB Montenegro apps published under Asseco package namespaces). This is a reliable indirect way to attribute a bank's channel stack to a supplier even when neither party issues a press release; developer/publisher changes signal a vendor switch.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica - e-banking platform migration notices (Halcom -> eMon OfficeBanking)
why_relevant: Customer-facing migration notices on a private bank's own site are one of the few public disclosures of a supplier swap at a Montenegrin bank (here: away from Halcom's platform to an OfficeBanking-family product). Such projects reliably accompany internal reorganisation and vendor-side hiring.

source_name: Halcom - bank coverage / supported-banks pages and regional site
why_relevant: Halcom publicly states it operates across seven monetary systems including Montenegro and lists partner banks; its bank lists and CA (certification) pages let you attribute corporate e-banking and e-signature infrastructure at ME banks, and detect losses of customers (as at Erste ME).

source_name: Poslovi Infostud - regional job board carrying ME/regional vendor vacancies (e.g. Payten ATM technician)
why_relevant: Vendor vacancies (ATM tehnicar at Payten d.o.o., POS field service, implementation consultants) are the most granular public evidence of a supplier scaling a Montenegro/regional service organisation. Job text often names the bank programme or terminal estate being supported.

source_name: Zaposli.ME - Montenegrin employment portal (IT category)
why_relevant: Described as the most-visited Montenegrin employment portal; the IT category is where a vendor opening a Podgorica office or country-manager role would advertise locally.

source_name: Radnik.me - Montenegrin job portal, Podgorica listings
why_relevant: Second Montenegrin job aggregator; redundancy matters because vendor ads are posted unevenly across ME portals and expire quickly.

source_name: Prekoveze.me - Montenegrin employment site (Podgorica ads)
why_relevant: Additional ME-domestic vacancy source described as a leading employment site in Montenegro; useful for SME integrators and field-service roles that never reach LinkedIn.

source_name: Berza rada - Montenegrin employment portal with employer profile pages
why_relevant: Hosts per-employer profile pages ('poslodavci/...'), which give a persistent handle for tracking a given vendor's hiring cadence in Montenegro rather than only single ads.

source_name: CRPS - Central Register of Business Entities of Montenegro (company search)
why_relevant: Authoritative registry for a foreign vendor incorporating a Montenegrin subsidiary or registering a branch/representative office ('predstavnistvo stranog drustva'), and for changes of executive director. This is the hardest evidence of a supplier 'opening a Podgorica office' and of who its legal representative (de facto country manager) is.

source_name: eUprava Montenegro - business registration service pages
why_relevant: Explains the registration procedures and the exact legal form names used for foreign presence in Montenegro, which supplies the correct query vocabulary for CRPS lookups and for spotting a vendor's first legal footprint.

source_name: Bankar.me - 'KOMPANIJE' (company news) section
why_relevant: Montenegro's dedicated banking/finance portal; the company-news category is where supplier press releases about ME bank implementations, new local offices and appointments get republished, including named foreign technology partners on central-bank-coordinated programmes (instant payments, ISO 20022, SEPA).

source_name: Digitalizuj.Me - Montenegrin ICT/digital-economy news portal
why_relevant: Covers the domestic IT-company layer (cluster analyses, company growth, hiring waves) in local language; complements Bankar.me by covering the supplier side rather than the bank side.

source_name: Coreit d.o.o. Podgorica - Montenegrin systems integrator (company profile via EMIS)
why_relevant: Coreit is a Podgorica consulting/system-integration firm that states it runs IT projects for financial institutions; profile pages of this kind give key executives and financials, which is how you detect leadership change and growth at private integrators that publish little themselves.

source_name: Mastercard Montenegro - acquiring banks page ('Banke prihvatioci')
why_relevant: Scheme-side listing of which Montenegrin banks acquire card payments; the acquiring set defines which banks buy POS estates and processing, i.e. the demand side of this cell. Changes to the list indicate a bank entering/exiting acquiring, which is normally accompanied by a supplier selection and hiring.

source_name: Regional card-personalisation bureaux serving ME banks (Zeta, SIS, Cards Print - RS-based)
why_relevant: No Montenegrin card-personalisation bureau surfaced; the function appears to be served from Serbia/region or in-house at banks. These vendors' service pages (including in-house personalisation leasing models) are the practical place where a Montenegrin bank customer or a new local engagement would appear.

source_name: Chamber of Economy of Montenegro (Privredna komora Crne Gore) - boards and member communications
why_relevant: Sector boards and member news are a route to identifying which supplier companies are institutionally active in Montenegro and who represents them; board membership changes are a low-noise leadership signal.

source_name: Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (UBCG) — Association of Montenegrin Banks, official site
why_relevant: The single canonical enumeration of licensed banks operating in Montenegro (11 member banks as of 2025-2026) plus the Association's own governance: Assembly, Upravni odbor (Management Board) president, Director. Association presidency turns over roughly annually and is itself a bank-CEO-level leadership signal; the member list is the actor universe that every other A5 cell (jobs, hiring, leadership moves) must be joined against. Site URL is inferred from the acronym and news references and is NOT confirmed — treat as hypothesis and resolve via the news/registry candidates in this slice.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore — Odbor udruženja bankarstva, drugih finansijskih organizacija i osiguranja (Chamber of Economy, Banking/Finance/Insurance Association Board)
source_subtype: chamber of commerce sectoral board roster
why_relevant: Publishes the full named roster of the banking/finance/insurance board — one designated senior person per institution, with their employer, plus the board president/deputy and the Chamber secretary contact. Observed roster includes Miloš Miketić (Lovćen banka, president), Boris Čabrilo (Addiko), Dino Redžepagić (CKB), Marko Čelebić (NLB), Mensur Markišić (Ziraat), Milijana Živković (Adriatic Bank), Mladen Rabrenović (Zapad banka), plus regulators (CBCG, Komisija za tržište kapitala, Agencija za nadzor osiguranja) and payments/fintech actors (Monte Credit, Moj kredit, Montenegro Transfers, CKDD). Diffing this page over time surfaces individual moves AND institution entries/exits.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore — organi Komore (Skupština, Upravni odbor, Nadzorni odbor, Predsjednik)
why_relevant: Chamber-level governance pages name who sits on the Assembly/Management/Supervisory boards and the President — bank and payment-company executives regularly hold these seats, so elections here are directly reportable leadership signals and confirm who currently represents each institution externally.

source_name: Montenegrin Foreign Investors' Council (MFIC) / Savjet stranih investitora — Banking Committee and Board
why_relevant: MFIC enumerates the foreign-owned banking/payments actor set and their designated senior representatives. Observed: Banking Committee permanent members Addiko Bank, Erste Bank, Hipotekarna banka, NLB Banka, CKB and Mastercard — a rare explicit link between a card scheme and the local bank set. MFIC presidency is held by a bank CEO (Tamaš Kamaraši, CKB), so board elections here double as leadership-move signals; MFIC annual White Book also names committee chairs.

source_name: AmCham Montenegro — Board of Governors
why_relevant: AmCham's Board of Governors is an elected body whose seats are held by named executives with employer attribution (observed: president of the management board of Lovćen banka ad Podgorica; EPAM Systems Montenegro; Sava osiguranje). Elections are annual/biennial and reported — a clean leadership-move feed plus a cross-sector actor map that catches payments-adjacent IT firms banks buy from.

source_name: AmCham Montenegro — member area / user registry
why_relevant: Member-company listing with contact persons; if it is public it enumerates AmCham's banking/payments/IT membership. Appears to be an account-gated area (a /register/ page exists), so likely partially restricted.

source_name: Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore (UPCG) — Montenegrin Employers Federation, Upravni odbor
why_relevant: Employer-side social partner whose Management Board and presidency are elected at a quadrennial assembly (Slobodan Mikavica elected president 2023-04-13; Slaviša Šćekić assembly president). Board seats are held by company executives including financial-sector firms; UPCG is also the counterpart on collective-bargaining and labour/jobs policy — directly on-topic for the jobs/hiring workstream.

source_name: Asocijacija menadžera Crne Gore (AMM) — membership list and Upravni odbor
why_relevant: AMM is a personal-membership executives' association: its member and board listings map named individuals to employers across banking (observed: Damir Ivaštinović / Erste banka, Ana Cmiljanić / Razvojna banka CG, Biljana Vujović / Addiko Bank). AMM also spawns sub-bodies — a CFO Association and a 'digital team' — whose launches are themselves organization-change and hiring signals. Individual-level granularity that institutional sites do not provide.

source_name: CFO Asocijacija Crne Gore (Association of Financial Directors) — newly formed AMM offshoot
source_subtype: professional association (emerging) — covered via trade press
why_relevant: A brand-new body enumerating the CFOs of Montenegrin institutions including banks — the CFO layer is exactly where finance-function hiring and reorganisation shows up first, and the founding board (Ivaštinović/Erste, Cmiljanić/Razvojna banka, Vujović/Addiko) is a ready-made contact map. As a new association it has no stable homepage found yet; track via AMM and trade press.

source_name: CBCG Fintech Hub — Central Bank of Montenegro fintech portal
why_relevant: Regulator-run hub that convenes and lists fintech/payment-institution actors and working groups. In the absence of a standalone Montenegrin fintech association, this is the de facto enumeration point for the fintech actor universe and for named working-group participants — a pointer that feeds the payments side of the actor map.
